## Project identity

| | |
|---|---|
| **Title** | QUBI: Kompetenzorientiertes, modulares Lernen in Quantitativer Biologie |
| **Leads** | Claudia Bank; Stephan Peischl |
| **Programme** | BSc Major Biologie (Phil.-nat.), new Anhang 1 from **HS26** |
| **Courses** | **Quantitative Biologie I & II** (2+2 ECTS) = Pflichtmodul **1D Themen der Biologie** (4 ECTS) |
| **Slot** | Year 1, parallel to central methods courses |
| **Impulses** | Curriculum; digital materials; competence orientation; practice link; interdisciplinarity; study entry |

This repo is the authoring hub for **QuBi I** (HS; ecology → evo → establishment/rescue → microbiome data skills).

---

## Problem the proposal solves

- Parallel stats/programming courses → redundancy, uneven standards, cost
- Central methods courses feel abstract / demotivating for biologists
- Biology’s own stats course worked pedagogically but does not scale as an island
- Need: keep **central** methods teaching, add a **bridge** course that reconnects methods to biology

## Stated goals (compressed)

1. Replace bio-only stats/programming islands with shared central offerings  
2. Build accompanying **Quantitative Biology** across the first two semesters  
3. Raise **competence orientation** (modelling, simulation, data analysis)  
4. Support **study entry** and early research realism  
5. Pilot **interdisciplinary** coupling (bio ↔ maths/stats/CS), transferable + linked to **Schatztruhe**

---

## What we promised to build

- Modular QuBi course **in parallel** with programming (then stats) service courses
- **Same biological models/stories reused** across methods contexts (e.g. simulate in programming phase; revisit statistically later)
- Curated **real research-adjacent datasets** + reusable digital modules (R / Python / notebooks)
- Two work streams: (1) teaching datasets, (2) digital practice modules on ILIAS + repos
- Sustainability via curriculum embedding + Schatztruhe deposit; maintenance by QuBi instructors

## Curriculum neighbourhood (HS26)

Year 1 replaces older programming/maths arrangement with e.g.:

- Basics of Programming and Data Science  
- Statistik für Naturwissenschaften  
- **+ QuBi I & II** as the biology bridge  

Year 2 shifts modelling/stats offerings (incl. Mathematische Modellierung in der Biologie). QuBi must **complement**, not duplicate, those courses.

---

## Implications for QuBi I materials (this repo)

| Proposal emphasis | How QuBi I responds |
|---|---|
| Biology first, methods as tools | Bajau hook; Gause / Isle Royale / rescue / microbiome tables |
| Parallel to programming course | Explicit function → vector → loop → plot engine |
| Competence / practice | Checkpoints A–D (practical + short talk), not one final mega-project only |
| Real / research-like data | Digitized classic + field series; open microbiome tables (W11–13) |
| Modular digital materials | Quarto site, week folders, notebooks, GitHub Pages deploy |
| AI / modern scientific practice | Course [AI policy](ai-policy.qmd) |
| MfB competence landscape | Touch many codes; don’t claim full coverage — [MfB map](mfb-alignment.qmd) |
| Schatztruhe / transfer | Keep modules reusable; clear READMEs; cite data |

**Do not:** rebuild a full stats course or a full programming course inside QuBi.

---

## Resources (proposal)

- **48 PP** total (36 PP developer/coordinator ~Jun 2026–Jul 2027; 12 PP teaching capacity for QuBi while old stats still runs)
- Kick-off with VRL Lehre after funding confirmation

---

## Collaborator checklist

When adding a week, ask:

1. Does this **bridge** a methods idea to a biological question/dataset?  
2. Does it reuse the simulation / data engine students already know?  
3. Is it something the parallel programming/stats course is **not** already owning?  
4. Can a checkpoint product show a **competence** (model, sim, figure, honest limit)?  
5. Is the material modular enough to become a Schatztruhe-style unit later?
